inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate the admin console as a functional SPA.

Scoring criteria:
- 5: Fully functional React SPA with root element, JS bundles loaded, clear navigation for realm/user/client/role/group management, sidebar and content area rendered.
- 4: React SPA loads with JS bundles, navigation covers most admin areas but may be missing 1-2 sections.
- 3: SPA shell renders with React root and some JS, navigation structure partially present but incomplete.
- 2: HTML loads with React root element but JS bundles fail or navigation is minimal/broken.
- 1: Page loads but is mostly static HTML, no SPA behavior or React rendering.
- 0: No admin console page, returns error, or completely empty.

nodes.description: Login page renders with username/password form fields and proper HTML structure

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate the login page quality.

Scoring criteria:
- 5: Complete login form with username input, password input, submit button, proper form action, CSRF protection, and clean semantic HTML structure.
- 4: Login form with username/password/submit and form action present, minor structural issues (e.g., missing CSRF or non-semantic tags).
- 3: Login form with username and password fields and a submit button, but form action missing or incorrect, or HTML poorly structured.
- 2: Page has input fields but missing submit button or password field, or form is non-functional.
- 1: Page renders but contains only minimal HTML with no recognizable login form elements.
- 0: No login page, returns error, or blank page.

nodes.description: OAuth2/OIDC protocol implementation follows standards: proper token format, discovery, error handling

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate OIDC/OAuth2 standards compliance based on observed API responses.

Scoring criteria:
- 5: Fully compliant — discovery document has all required fields per OpenID Connect Discovery spec, JWKS correctly exposes keys with proper kid/alg/use, token responses follow RFC 6749 exactly, error responses use standard error/error_description format.
- 4: Mostly compliant — discovery and JWKS correct, minor deviations in token or error response format (e.g., extra non-standard fields).
- 3: Core flows work — tokens issued correctly, discovery present, but JWKS has issues (missing fields) or error responses deviate from RFC format.
- 2: Partial implementation — some endpoints work but discovery incomplete, JWKS missing or malformed, or token format non-standard.
- 1: Minimal — only token endpoint partially works, no proper discovery or JWKS.
- 0: No OIDC implementation or all endpoints return errors.

nodes.description: Multi-tenant realm isolation is properly architected with clean data separation

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate the multi-tenant realm architecture design.

Scoring criteria:
- 6: Excellent — complete realm isolation with realm ID foreign keys on all resource tables, no cross-realm data leakage possible, clean tenant-scoped queries, realm-aware caching, and consistent realm parameter propagation through all service layers.
- 5: Strong — realm scoping correct on all major entities, data isolation enforced, minor gaps in edge-case resources (e.g., shared global config not realm-scoped).
- 4: Good — most resources properly realm-scoped, data model has realm FK on core tables, but some secondary tables or caches lack realm awareness.
- 3: Adequate — realm concept exists and core entities are scoped, but isolation is incomplete (some queries don't filter by realm, or some tables share data across realms).
- 2: Weak — realm exists as a concept but scoping is inconsistent, multiple tables lack realm FK, cross-realm data exposure possible.
- 1: Minimal — single hardcoded realm or realm parameter exists but is not enforced in data access.
- 0: No multi-tenancy — single flat namespace with no realm concept.

nodes.description: Authentication flow engine: composable sub-flows, conditionals, configurable requirements

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate the authentication flow architecture.

Scoring criteria:
- 8: Exceptional — flow processor iterates execution list, sub-flows supported recursively with correct nesting, all 4 requirement types (REQUIRED/ALTERNATIVE/CONDITIONAL/DISABLED) implemented with correct logic, authenticator providers are pluggable via SPI, flow bindings configurable per-client, and execution ordering is manageable.
- 7: Excellent — all 4 requirement types work, sub-flow recursion supported, authenticator providers pluggable, minor gaps in client-level flow binding or execution ordering.
- 6: Strong — flow processor with execution iteration, 3-4 requirement types implemented correctly, sub-flows supported but limited nesting depth, authenticator providers configurable.
- 5: Good — flow processor exists, REQUIRED and ALTERNATIVE work correctly, sub-flows partially supported, authenticator providers are selectable but not fully pluggable.
- 4: Adequate — basic flow execution with REQUIRED/ALTERNATIVE, no sub-flow support, authenticator selection from a fixed list.
- 3: Basic — single linear authentication chain, only REQUIRED requirement type, no sub-flows or alternatives.
- 2: Minimal — hardcoded authentication steps, no flow abstraction, no requirement model.
- 1: Rudimentary — single username/password check with no flow concept.
- 0: No authentication flow architecture.

nodes.description: SPI plugin system: Provider/ProviderFactory pattern with discovery mechanism

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate the SPI/plugin extensibility system.

Scoring criteria:
- 7: Comprehensive — ProviderFactory pattern with proper lifecycle (create/init/close), all 5 extension points pluggable (authenticators, protocol mappers, user storage, identity providers, event listeners), service discovery/registration mechanism (e.g., ServiceLoader or custom registry), and provider configuration persistence.
- 6: Strong — ProviderFactory pattern used, 4-5 extension points pluggable, discovery mechanism present, minor gaps in lifecycle management or configuration.
- 5: Good — clear SPI interfaces for 3-4 extension points, factory pattern used, basic registration mechanism but no auto-discovery.
- 4: Adequate — SPI interfaces for 2-3 extension points, factory pattern partially applied, manual registration required.
- 3: Basic — some extensibility via interfaces for 1-2 areas, no factory pattern or formal SPI structure.
- 2: Minimal — extensibility exists via class inheritance/override in 1 area, no formal plugin system.
- 1: Rudimentary — all providers hardcoded, extensibility only via source code modification.
- 0: No extensibility architecture.

nodes.description: Password hashing security: Argon2id with appropriate parameters, random salt

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate password security implementation.

Scoring criteria:
- 6: Excellent — Argon2id (or bcrypt/scrypt) with strong parameters (memory>=4MB, iterations>=3 for Argon2, cost>=12 for bcrypt), cryptographically random salt >=16 bytes per password, plaintext never stored or logged, password policy validators composable (chain of validators), and credential storage uses dedicated entity with versioning.
- 5: Strong — secure adaptive hash used with reasonable parameters, random salt, no plaintext, policy validators exist but not fully composable (e.g., fixed chain).
- 4: Good — secure hash algorithm used, proper salting, no plaintext storage, basic password policy validation (length/complexity) but not composable.
- 3: Adequate — password hashing present (e.g., PBKDF2) but parameters may be weak, salting exists, basic length validation only.
- 2: Weak — hashing used but with weak algorithm (MD5/SHA1) or insufficient iterations, salt may be short or static, minimal validation.
- 1: Poor — passwords hashed but with known vulnerabilities (no salt, weak hash), or plaintext visible in logs/debug output.
- 0: Passwords stored in plaintext or no hashing mechanism.

nodes.description: JWT signing quality, key management, algorithm support

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate JWT/token security architecture.

Scoring criteria:
- 6: Excellent — tokens signed with asymmetric keys (RS256+), key rotation supported with graceful rollover (old keys still verify during transition), token lifespans configurable per-realm and per-client, token revocation implemented (revocation endpoint + revoked token checking), and refresh token rotation enabled.
- 5: Strong — asymmetric signing, key rotation mechanism exists, configurable lifespans, revocation endpoint present but may lack proactive checking on all paths.
- 4: Good — asymmetric signing (RS256), key rotation possible but manual, configurable lifespans at realm level, basic revocation via session invalidation.
- 3: Adequate — asymmetric signing works, no key rotation, lifespans configurable at realm level only, no dedicated revocation mechanism (relies on expiration).
- 2: Weak — symmetric signing (HS256 with shared secret), no key rotation, fixed or hardcoded lifespans, no revocation.
- 1: Poor — tokens generated but signing is weak or misconfigured, no lifespan management.
- 0: No token signing, tokens are unsigned/unverified, or no JWT implementation.

nodes.description: API error responses: informative, consistent, safe

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate API error handling quality.

Scoring criteria:
- 5: Excellent — Admin API consistently returns {errorMessage} format, OAuth/OIDC endpoints return {error, error_description} per RFC 6749, correct HTTP status codes throughout (400/401/403/404/409), error messages are informative for debugging but never expose stack traces, internal paths, SQL, or sensitive data.
- 4: Strong — both error formats used correctly in their respective APIs, proper status codes, minor cases of overly generic or slightly inconsistent messages.
- 3: Adequate — error format mostly consistent within each API, correct status codes for common cases, but some endpoints return wrong format or leak minor internal details.
- 2: Weak — error format inconsistent (mixing Admin and OAuth formats), some incorrect status codes (e.g., 500 instead of 400), or error messages expose internal class names.
- 1: Poor — errors mostly return generic 500 with stack traces or HTML error pages instead of JSON.
- 0: No structured error handling — raw exceptions or no error responses.

nodes.description: Liquibase changelogs well-structured, idempotent, version-tracked

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate database migration and schema quality.

Scoring criteria:
- 5: Excellent — Liquibase or Flyway changelogs used with sequential versioning, migrations are ordered and idempotent (re-runnable without error), schema is normalized (3NF+), foreign keys have indexes, naming conventions consistent, and migration includes rollback support.
- 4: Strong — migration tool used with versioned changelogs, migrations ordered, schema mostly normalized, FK indexes present, minor naming inconsistencies.
- 3: Adequate — migration tool present, changelogs exist but ordering may have gaps, schema has some denormalization, most FK indexes present.
- 2: Weak — migrations exist but are ad-hoc SQL scripts without proper versioning or ordering, schema has redundancy, missing FK indexes.
- 1: Poor — raw SQL scripts with no migration framework, schema created manually, no versioning or idempotency.
- 0: No database migration — schema created inline in application code or not at all.

nodes.description: SAML 2.0 implementation quality: XML signing, encryption, metadata, bindings

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate SAML 2.0 protocol implementation.

Scoring criteria:
- 5: Complete — XML signing with Exclusive C14N canonicalization, assertion encryption (AES-GCM or AES-CBC) supported, all 3 bindings implemented (HTTP-POST, HTTP-Redirect, SOAP), auto-generated SP/IdP metadata endpoint, multiple NameID formats supported (persistent, transient, email, unspecified).
- 4: Strong — XML signing correct, encryption supported, 2-3 bindings implemented, metadata auto-generated, at least 2 NameID formats.
- 3: Adequate — XML signing works, basic encryption, HTTP-POST binding functional, metadata partially auto-generated, 1-2 NameID formats.
- 2: Weak — SAML assertions generated but signing may use non-standard canonicalization, no encryption, single binding only, manual metadata configuration.
- 1: Minimal — basic SAML response generation without proper signing or encryption, no metadata endpoint.
- 0: No SAML implementation or non-functional.

nodes.description: Code organization, module separation, naming, maintainability

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate code maintainability and architecture quality.

Scoring criteria:
- 7: Exceptional — well-organized module structure with clear boundaries, consistent naming conventions (camelCase for Java, PascalCase for classes), strict separation of concerns (model/service/resource layers), clean build config (POM with managed dependencies, no version conflicts), meaningful abstractions (interfaces for services, DTOs for API boundaries), and low coupling between modules.
- 6: Excellent — clear module structure, consistent naming, proper layering, clean build, good abstractions with minor coupling issues between 1-2 modules.
- 5: Strong — organized modules, mostly consistent naming, separation of concerns followed, build config reasonable, some abstractions may be too thin or too thick.
- 4: Good — recognizable module structure, naming mostly consistent, layers exist but some business logic bleeds into resource/controller layer, build works but has minor issues.
- 3: Adequate — some module organization, naming conventions partially followed, basic layering exists but not strictly enforced, build functional.
- 2: Weak — flat or poorly organized structure, inconsistent naming, business logic mixed across layers, build config messy.
- 1: Poor — monolithic code with no module separation, arbitrary naming, no architectural layers.
- 0: No discernible architecture — single-file or chaotic code organization.

nodes.description: Account Console: self-service UI for password, sessions, linked accounts

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate the account console (self-service user portal).

Scoring criteria:
- 5: Fully functional React SPA with client-side routing, sections for personal info editing, security settings (password change, 2FA), active sessions management, and authorized applications listing — all sections accessible and interactive.
- 4: React SPA with routing, 3-4 sections present and functional, minor UI gaps (e.g., one section not fully interactive).
- 3: SPA renders with some sections visible, routing partially works, 2-3 sections present but some non-functional or read-only.
- 2: Page loads with React root, minimal content, only 1 section partially working, routing broken or absent.
- 1: Page loads but is mostly static or empty, no functional self-service features.
- 0: No account console, returns error, or page is blank.

nodes.description: Email templates for verification, password reset, admin actions

inputs.rubric_prompt:
Evaluate email template implementation.

Scoring criteria:
- 4: Complete — FreeMarker (or equivalent) templates exist for all 4 email types (verification, password reset, execute-actions, org invitation), each template includes action token link placeholder (e.g., ${link}), templates are i18n-ready with message bundle references, and HTML email structure is clean.
- 3: Good — templates for 3 of 4 email types, action token links present, basic i18n support (at least locale-aware).
- 2: Partial — templates for 1-2 email types, action links present in those templates, no i18n or hardcoded strings.
- 1: Minimal — one template exists but is plain text only, no action token links, no i18n.
- 0: No email templates implemented.
